back_blocks.md: **Polarisation** is the restriction of the oscillations of a transverse wave to **one plane**, while the oscillations remain perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer.

cards.back_md: **Polarisation** is the restriction of the oscillations of a transverse wave to **one plane**, while the oscillations remain perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer.

front_blocks.md: Why can only transverse waves be polarised, and not longitudinal waves?

back_blocks.md: Polarisation restricts oscillation to a single plane perpendicular to the direction of travel. **Longitudinal** waves oscillate parallel to the direction of travel, so there is no perpendicular plane to restrict, meaning they cannot be polarised.

cards.back_md: Polarisation restricts oscillation to a single plane perpendicular to the direction of travel. **Longitudinal** waves oscillate parallel to the direction of travel, so there is no perpendicular plane to restrict, meaning they cannot be polarised.

front_blocks.md: How does a polarising filter produce a polarised wave from an unpolarised wave?

back_blocks.md: A **polariser** consists of many parallel tiny slits. It only transmits waves oscillating **parallel** to the direction of the slits; waves in other planes are blocked.

front_blocks.md: Why do polaroid sunglasses with vertically oriented filters reduce glare?

back_blocks.md: Their transmission axis is **vertical**, so they block **horizontally polarised light**, only allowing vertically polarised light through.

front_blocks.md: If unpolarised light of intensity *I*<sub>0</sub> passes through a single polariser, the transmitted intensity falls to **..........** of *I*<sub>0</sub> (the half rule).

back_blocks.md: If unpolarised light of intensity *I*<sub>0</sub> passes through a single polariser, the transmitted intensity falls to **half** of *I*<sub>0</sub> (the half rule).

back_blocks.md: θ is the angle between the transmission axes of the **analyser** and the **polariser**.

cards.front_md: State **Malus's law**, and define the angle θ in the equation.
cards.back_md:
$I = I_{0} \mathrm{cos}^{2} ( θ )$

θ is the angle between the transmission axes of the **analyser** and the **polariser**.

front_blocks.md: Rotating an analyser by 90° relative to the polariser will still transmit some light.

back_blocks.md: At 90°, cos<sup>2</sup>(90°) = 0, so **no light** is transmitted — all the polarised light is absorbed by the analyser.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Rotating an analyser by 90° relative to the polariser will still transmit some light.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

At 90°, cos<sup>2</sup>(90°) = 0, so **no light** is transmitted — all the polarised light is absorbed by the analyser.
